claim: ONE FIX with VAL-R5-01 (model). V07 §3.5a (4) (l. 1604-1615) reads every palisade as 'a wall laid after the raised way (§2.7's support step (6) (d))' and keeps a crossing station only for a raised way carried down from a CITY. The base gives a crossing station to every raised way created across a standing wall, a hand aqueduct included: §7.1 (l. 10441-10443) reads 'a course meeting an enceinte's trace comes down to a ground vertex before it …, while an aqueduct crosses a wall by an arch in the curtain, never a gate'; §4.8 *Gates* (l. 7668-7673) has 'by hand an aqueduct, §7.1' take the crossing as a wall opening; and §2.7's support step (3) holds that station. The palisade is an `Enceinte` (V07 §3.4 step 7), and V07 (1) admits a hand aqueduct at every rung. So on a palisaded village, a hand aqueduct drawn across the standing palisade gets a station by the base. Its stretch is held while the deck stands, so V07 §3.4 (8)'s decay passes over it, and it is taken back into the line as its support whenever VS3 re-lays the trace (§2.7 (6)). V07 instead treats the station as 'a support whose `state` is absent', abuts it and calls it 'never a gate', with no station kept. A station no stretch lies under becomes a pier with its own ring and `state`, so the two builds differ in the `supports` record, in the decay and in V04's reconcile. V07 also calls the carried-down station's 'raised gate … or the aqueduct's arch' 'the one gate at a support the palisade carries', but the base says an aqueduct's arch is 'not a gate (no portal, no gate law)' (§4.8; V06 §3.7.6 (5)), and T-V7-48 counts only the raised gate. 'A raised way crossing the circuit makes no gate (its deck passes over)' holds only for a raised way the palisade is laid after, because a hand raised road comes down before the trace (§7.1). Separately, and minor: 'The trace passes beneath an `open` span as an ordinary stretch' leaves out (6) (d)'s soffit cap.
required_change: V07 §3.5a (4): (a) Replace 'The palisade is a wall laid after the raised way (§2.7's support step (6) (d)):' with 'A palisade laid after a raised way — VS3's trace at generation and at every derivation that re-lays it, or a palisade T3 `wall` draws — runs on beneath its deck (§2.7's support step (6) (d)):'. (b) Replace 'The trace passes beneath an `open` span as an ordinary stretch' with 'The trace passes beneath an `open` span as an ordinary stretch, its top no higher than the span's soffit (§2.7's support step (6) (d))'. (c) Replace 'A raised way carried down (V07 §3.12) whose crossing station stands on the enceinte that becomes the palisade keeps that station as standing fabric — its support the band's stretch under the deck, held while the deck stands, with its raised gate whose tower carries the deck or the aqueduct's arch (§2.7's support step (3)) — the one gate at a support the palisade carries.' with 'A raised way created across the standing palisade keeps its crossing station (§2.7's support step (3)). This covers a hand aqueduct, which crosses by an arch in the curtain (§7.1; a hand raised road comes down before the trace instead). It also covers a raised way carried down (V07 §3.12) whose station stands on the enceinte that becomes the palisade. The station's support is the band's stretch under the deck, held while the deck stands and taken back into the line as its support at every derivation that re-lays the trace (§2.7's support step (6)). A carried-down raised gate, whose tower carries the deck, is the one gate at a support the palisade carries. An aqueduct's arch is no gate: no portal, no gate law (§4.8 *Gates*).' §3.17's row 'a raised way over the palisade' adds '; a hand aqueduct across the standing palisade crossing it at one station by its arch (V07 §3.5a (4))'. T-V7-48 adds 'a hand aqueduct drawn across the VILLAGE fixture's standing palisade — one crossing station on the trace, its stretch the station's support and held (no `breached` or `dismantled` there while the deck stands) through a village epoch whose decay breaches the palisade, no gate counted for its arch, and the station taken back into the line after Regenerate (keep)'. The model's side is VAL-R5-01.

claim: R5-06 (VAF-R4T-01) gave T-V7-69 (c) (V07 l. 3702) V01 §3.16 (5)'s count at the village rungs, with two cases: "on a VILLAGE fixture whose calamity names more ends than k (every named end struck) and on a fire whose order ends before k (the shortfall reported)". T-V7-69's fixture list holds neither. It names "THORP (P = 1, 40), HAMLET and VILLAGE (P = 1 499) fixtures — … each look kind previewed … and, from M-SF, a dossier fixture carrying each mapped condition, among them a disaster whose rebuild Works begin on some of an end's buildings inside its weeks". A preview has no targets, so it cannot name ends. A village fire's order ends before k only on a village where an end has no `neighbours` unit (V07 §5.6 (3), l. 3480–3485: no plot sharing a boundary or a way segment with another end's). No fixture is said to have that shape. This is R5-10's class: a test names a case that no fixture list carries, as VAP-r4-05 was at the town rungs, where V08 §7.1 now names `town-1`'s two banks. The test text states the cases, so the grade is minor.
required_change: T-V7-69's fixture list: after "among them a disaster whose rebuild Works begin on some of an end's buildings inside its weeks" add "; and two test-side mutations of one of V07 §7's frozen small-dossier VILLAGE fixtures, each from M-SF — a calamity whose `targets` name uses on more ends than its severity's share k of the village's units, and a fire at severity 1 whose `targets` name a use on an end that no other end neighbours (V07 §5.6 (3)'s `neighbours`: an end parted from the rest by a water face or by land no plot of either touches), its order ending at that end before k, the harness asserting the end's isolation before the clause reads it".

claim: V07 §4.5's crisis line (l. 3138–3144) gives a disaster's `VillageEnd` and a famine's `VillageField` "V09 §4.21.12 (4)'s `info.crisis.ruinedFor` row ("For now: Ruined quarters, the mill-end fire, weeks 30–34")"; W74 (l. 282) "the crisis line's V09 `info.crisis.ruinedFor`"; T-V7-69 (e) (l. 3702) "carries `info.crisis.ruinedFor`" — one form. Round 5's V09 §4.21.12 (4) gives the row five (open, unnamed, neither, preview), and V03 was conformed ("in its forms", l. 198; "under a preview `ruinedForPreview`", l. 2322); V07, the village restatement (R5-01 (2) (a)), was not. V07 §4.5 states "a preview never handing over" and T-V7-69 previews every look kind at the village rungs, where a preview has no condition or weeks. The cited home states the forms, so a builder following the citation gets them: a restatement differing in form.
required_change: V07 §4.5: "V09 §4.21.12 (4)'s `info.crisis.ruinedFor` row ("For now: Ruined quarters, the mill-end fire, weeks 30–34"), the one row" → "V09 §4.21.12 (4)'s `info.crisis.ruinedFor` row ("For now: Ruined quarters, the mill-end fire, weeks 30–34") in the form that section chooses — `ruinedForOpen`, `ruinedForUnnamed` or `ruinedForUnnamedOpen` for a look with no `untilWeek`, no name or neither, `ruinedForPreview` under a preview —, the one row"; W74: "the crisis line's V09 `info.crisis.ruinedFor`" → "the crisis line's V09 `info.crisis.ruinedFor` in its forms (V09 §4.21.12 (4))"; T-V7-69 (e): "carries `info.crisis.ruinedFor` while the look stands" → "carries `info.crisis.ruinedFor` in the form V09 §4.21.12 (4) chooses (under a preview `ruinedForPreview`) while the look stands".
